newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept real earnings rose 0.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept real earnings rose 0.8 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 0.8 percent in September, the Labor Department said Wednesday.
The September increase followed a revised 1.2 percent gain in August real average weekly earnings.
Previously, the department reported that August real earnings rose 0.7 percent.

The September rise stems from a 0.6 percent rise in average weekly hours, a 0.5 percent increase in average hourly earnings and a 0.3 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.
Real average weekly earnings in September were up 1.4 percent from September last year, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $258.67 in September, versus $256.69 in August and $255.34 in September 1995.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $413.62 in September, compared with $409.17 in August and $396.29 in September last year.
